left: # Test-Driven Development (TDD)
right: # Test-Driven Development (TDD)

left: ## Overview
right: ## Overview

left: Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.
right: Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

left: **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.
right: **Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

left: **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**
right: **Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

left: ## When to Use
right: ## When to Use

left: **Always:**
right: **Always:**

left: - New features
right: - New features

left: - Bug fixes
right: - Bug fixes

left: - Refactoring
right: - Refactoring

left: - Behavior changes
right: - Behavior changes

left: **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
right: **Exceptions (ask your human partner):**

left: - Throwaway prototypes
right: - Throwaway prototypes

left: - Generated code
right: - Generated code

left: - Configuration files
right: - Configuration files

left: Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.
right: Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

left: ## The Iron Law
right: ## The Iron Law

left: NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
right: NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST

left: Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.
right: Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

left: **No exceptions:**
right: **No exceptions:**

left: - Don't keep it as "reference"
right: - Don't keep it as "reference"

left: - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
right: - Don't "adapt" it while writing tests

left: - Don't look at it
right: - Don't look at it

left: - Delete means delete
right: - Delete means delete

left: Implement fresh from tests. Period.
right: Implement fresh from tests. Period.

left: ## Red-Green-Refactor
right: ## Red-Green-Refactor

left: Work one behavior at a time, in this order: RED, Verify RED, GREEN, Verify GREEN,
right: Work one behavior at a time: RED, Verify RED, GREEN, Verify GREEN,

left: REFACTOR, then the next failing test.
right: then REFACTOR while keeping tests green. Repeat with the next failing test.

right: ### RED - Write Failing Test

right: Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

left: ## Good Tests
right: ## Good Tests

left: - **Minimal:** one thing. "and" in name? Split it.

left: - **Clear:** name describes behavior.

left: When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
right: When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:

left: - Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
right: - Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it

left: - Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
right: - Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior

left: - Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
right: - Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes

right: - Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

left: ## Common Rationalizations
right: ## Common Rationalizations

left: | Excuse | Reality |
right: | Excuse | Reality |

left: | "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
right: | "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |

left: | "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
right: | "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |

left: | "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
right: | "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |

left: | "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
right: | "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |

left: | "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
right: | "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |

left: | "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
right: | "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |

left: | "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
right: | "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |

left: | "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
right: | "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |

left: | "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
right: | "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |

left: | "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
right: | "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |

left: | "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |
right: | "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

left: ## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over
right: ## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

left: - Code before test
right: - Code before test

left: - Test after implementation
right: - Test after implementation

left: - Test passes immediately
right: - Test passes immediately

left: - Can't explain why test failed
right: - Can't explain why test failed

left: - Tests added "later"
right: - Tests added "later"

left: - Rationalizing "just this once"
right: - Rationalizing "just this once"

left: - "I already manually tested it"
right: - "I already manually tested it"

left: - "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
right: - "Tests after achieve the same purpose"

left: - "It's about spirit not ritual"
right: - "It's about spirit not ritual"

left: - "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
right: - "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"

left: - "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
right: - "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"

left: - "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
right: - "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"

left: - "This is different because..."
right: - "This is different because..."

left: **All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**
right: **All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

left: ## Verification Checklist
right: ## Verification Checklist

left: Before marking work complete:
right: Before marking work complete:

left: - [ ] Every new function/method has a test
right: - [ ] Every new function/method has a test

left: - [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
right: - [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing

left: - [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
right: - [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)

left: - [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
right: - [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test

left: - [ ] All tests pass
right: - [ ] All tests pass

left: - [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
right: - [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

left: - [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
right: - [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)

left: - [ ] Edge cases and errors covered
right: - [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

left: Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.
right: Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

left: ## When Stuck
right: ## When Stuck

left: | Problem | Solution |
right: | Problem | Solution |

left: | Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
right: | Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |

left: | Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
right: | Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |

left: | Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
right: | Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |

left: | Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |
right: | Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

left: ## Debugging Integration
right: ## Debugging Integration

left: Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.
right: Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

left: Never fix bugs without a test.
right: Never fix bugs without a test.

left: ## Final Rule
right: ## Final Rule

left: Production code → test exists and failed first
right: Production code → test exists and failed first

left: Otherwise → not TDD
right: Otherwise → not TDD

left: No exceptions without your human partner's permission.
right: No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

right: | "One more round will converge" | Past the cap, rounds don't converge — the failure is structural. Adjudicate and route. |

right: | "The reviewer will just find something new anyway" | Scoped re-reviews verify fixes; they cannot wander. New findings on untouched code go to the ledger, not the loop. |

right: | "This finding is obviously wrong, I'll drop it" | You adjudicate only at the cap, and every ruling is a ledger entry. Silent discards are forbidden. |

right: | "The fix was small, skip the re-review" | Unreviewed fixes are how regressions land. Every round ends with a scoped re-review. |

right: name: verification-before-completion

left: description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

left: # Verification Before Completion
right: # Verification Before Completion

left: ## Overview
right: ## Overview

left: **Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.
right: **Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

left: **Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**
right: **Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

left: ## The Iron Law
right: ## The Iron Law

left: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
right: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE

left: If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.
right: If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

left: ## The Gate Function
right: ## The Gate Function

left: BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:
right: BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

left: 1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
right: 1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?

left: 2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
right: 2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)

left: 3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
right: 3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures

left: 4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
right: 4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?

left: - If NO: State actual status with evidence
right: - If NO: State actual status with evidence

left: - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
right: - If YES: State claim WITH evidence

left: 5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim
right: 5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

left: Skip any step = lying, not verifying
right: Skip any step = lying, not verifying

left: ## Common Failures
right: ## Common Failures

left: | Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
right: | Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |

left: | Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
right: | Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |

left: | Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
right: | Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |

left: | Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
right: | Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |

left: | Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
right: | Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |

left: | Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
right: | Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |

left: | Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
right: | Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |

left: | Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |
right: | Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

left: ## Red Flags - STOP
right: ## Red Flags - STOP

left: - Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
right: - Using "should", "probably", "seems to"

left: - Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
right: - Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)

left: - About to commit/push/PR without verification
right: - About to commit/push/PR without verification

left: - Trusting agent success reports
right: - Trusting agent success reports

left: - Relying on partial verification
right: - Relying on partial verification

left: - Thinking "just this once"
right: - Thinking "just this once"

left: - Tired and wanting work over
right: - Tired and wanting work over

left: - **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**
right: - **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

left: ## Rationalization Prevention
right: ## Rationalization Prevention

left: | Excuse | Reality |
right: | Excuse | Reality |

left: | "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
right: | "Should work now" | RUN the verification |

left: | "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
right: | "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |

left: | "Just this once" | No exceptions |
right: | "Just this once" | No exceptions |

left: | "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
right: | "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |

left: | "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
right: | "Agent said success" | Verify independently |

left: | "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
right: | "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |

left: | "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
right: | "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |

left: | "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |
right: | "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

left: ## Key Patterns
right: ## Key Patterns

left: **Tests:**
right: **Tests:**

left: ✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
right: ✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"

left: ❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
right: ❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"

left: **Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
right: **Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**

left: ✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
right: ✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)

left: ❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
right: ❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)

left: **Build:**
right: **Build:**

left: ✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
right: ✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"

left: ❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
right: ❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)

left: **Requirements:**
right: **Requirements:**

left: ✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
right: ✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion

left: ❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
right: ❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"

left: **Agent delegation:**
right: **Agent delegation:**

right: ✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state

right: ❌ Trust agent report

right: ## When To Apply

right: - ANY variation of success/completion claims

left: | Excuse | Reality |

left: | "Close enough on spec compliance" | Reviewer found spec gaps = not done. Fix or hit the cap and adjudicate — those are the only exits. |
right: | "Close enough on spec compliance" | Reviewer found spec gaps = not done. Fix or hit the cap and adjudicate — those are the only exits. |

left: | "I'll fix it myself, dispatching is overhead" | Controller fixes pollute your context and skip review. Resume the implementer. |
right: | "I'll fix it myself, dispatching is overhead" | Controller fixes pollute your context and skip review. Resume the implementer. |

left: | "One more round will converge" | Past the cap, rounds don't converge — the failure is structural. Adjudicate and route. |
right: | "One more round will converge" | Past the cap, rounds don't converge — the failure is structural. Adjudicate and route. |

left: | "The reviewer will just find something new anyway" | Scoped re-reviews verify fixes; they cannot wander. New findings on untouched code go to the ledger, not the loop. |
right: | "The reviewer will just find something new anyway" | Scoped re-reviews verify fixes; they cannot wander. New findings on untouched code go to the ledger, not the loop. |

left: | "This finding is obviously wrong, I'll drop it" | You adjudicate only at the cap, and every ruling is a ledger entry. Silent discards are forbidden. |
right: | "This finding is obviously wrong, I'll drop it" | You adjudicate only at the cap, and every ruling is a ledger entry. Silent discards are forbidden. |

left: | "The fix was small, skip the re-review" | Unreviewed fixes are how regressions land. Every round ends with a scoped re-review. |
right: | "The fix was small, skip the re-review" | Unreviewed fixes are how regressions land. Every round ends with a scoped re-review. |

left: description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
right: description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

left: # Verification Before Completion
right: # Verification Before Completion

left: ## Overview
right: ## Overview

left: **Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.
right: **Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

left: **Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**
right: **Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

left: ## The Iron Law
right: ## The Iron Law

left: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
right: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE

left: If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.
right: If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

left: ## The Gate Function
right: ## The Gate Function

left: BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:
right: BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

left: 1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
right: 1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?

left: 2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
right: 2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)

left: 3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
right: 3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures

left: 4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
right: 4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?

left: - If NO: State actual status with evidence
right: - If NO: State actual status with evidence

left: - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
right: - If YES: State claim WITH evidence

left: 5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim
right: 5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

left: Skip any step = lying, not verifying
right: Skip any step = lying, not verifying

left: ## Common Failures
right: ## Common Failures

left: | Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
right: | Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |

left: | Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
right: | Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |

left: | Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
right: | Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |

left: | Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
right: | Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |

left: | Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
right: | Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |

left: | Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
right: | Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |

left: | Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
right: | Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |

left: | Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |
right: | Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

left: ## Red Flags - STOP
right: ## Red Flags - STOP

left: - Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
right: - Using "should", "probably", "seems to"

left: - Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
right: - Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)

left: - About to commit/push/PR without verification
right: - About to commit/push/PR without verification

left: - Trusting agent success reports
right: - Trusting agent success reports

left: - Relying on partial verification
right: - Relying on partial verification

left: - Thinking "just this once"
right: - Thinking "just this once"

left: - Tired and wanting work over
right: - Tired and wanting work over

left: - **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**
right: - **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

left: ## Rationalization Prevention
right: ## Rationalization Prevention

left: | Excuse | Reality |
right: | Excuse | Reality |

left: | "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
right: | "Should work now" | RUN the verification |

left: | "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
right: | "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |

left: | "Just this once" | No exceptions |
right: | "Just this once" | No exceptions |

left: | "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
right: | "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |

left: | "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
right: | "Agent said success" | Verify independently |

left: | "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
right: | "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |

left: | "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
right: | "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |

left: | "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |
right: | "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

left: ## Key Patterns
right: ## Key Patterns

left: **Tests:**
right: **Tests:**

left: ✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
right: ✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"

left: ❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
right: ❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"

left: **Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
right: **Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**

left: ✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
right: ✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)

left: ❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
right: ❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)

left: **Build:**
right: **Build:**

left: ✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
right: ✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"

left: ❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
right: ❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)

left: **Requirements:**
right: **Requirements:**

left: ✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
right: ✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion

left: ❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
right: ❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"

left: **Agent delegation:**
right: **Agent delegation:**

left: ✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
right: ✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state

left: ❌ Trust agent report
right: ❌ Trust agent report

left: ## When To Apply
right: ## When To Apply

left: **ALWAYS before:**
right: **ALWAYS before:**

left: - ANY variation of success/completion claims
right: - ANY variation of success/completion claims

left: - ANY expression of satisfaction
right: - ANY expression of satisfaction

left: - ANY positive statement about work state
right: - ANY positive statement about work state

left: - Committing, PR creation, task completion
right: - Committing, PR creation, task completion

left: - Moving to next task
right: - Moving to next task

left: - Delegating to agents
right: - Delegating to agents

left: **Rule applies to:**
right: **Rule applies to:**

left: - Exact phrases
right: - Exact phrases

left: - Paraphrases and synonyms
right: - Paraphrases and synonyms

left: - Implications of success
right: - Implications of success

left: - ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness
right: - ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness
